components: Compare a published direct free-neutron charge estimate to a supplied charge plane, conventional diagonal quotient, electromagnetic readout and valence dictionary. Fixing the positive scalar character h=3 gives a discrete nonzero gap; changing it admits inequivalent primitive ratios arbitrarily near zero without changing the quotient.

Two published appearance links constrain active flavor charges only under an exact unbroken U(1), definite-charge tags, neutral transfer in every propagation Kraus branch, and the supplied interpretation of the measurements.

Conserving total charge with reservoir exchange is compatible with nonzero appearance between differently charged flavors. Same-charge controls can have different dynamics and the same flavor table; connected active charges do not fix a common shift or the sterile sector.
candidates.declared_status: Conditional comparisons using published summaries as inputs; no new experiment or fit. The bulk-matter converted bound is not used as a second neutron anchor, and appearance counts are not treated as transition probabilities.
missing_bridges: Independently justify the scalar weight, charge lattice, electromagnetic normalization and composition dictionary before transferring the fixed-weight neutron comparison to physical charge selection.
Justify charge-sharp preparation and detection and bound hidden exchange before treating appearance as a charge-equality test; this does not determine a neutrino dynamics.

sources.text:
Inputs, not IDT outputs: the six one-family left-Weyl representations, the
ordinary anomaly conditions, one scalar doublet and charge-conserving Yukawa
links of probe_packet_charge_pairings. Use integer U(1) characters; q is the
quark-doublet character, h>0 the independently oriented scalar character.
Require the conventional diagonal Z6 quotient, q=1 mod 6, h=3 mod 6.
Supply a neutral lower Higgs component, T3 doublet eigenvalues ±1/2, and
electromagnetic readout T3+y/(2h). Identify proton/neutron charges with
the additive valence uud/udd charges. No particle, confinement, measurement
operator, or charge lattice normalization is derived from packet primitives.
Use electron units only when the electron is charged (3q+h nonzero).

With these inputs hydrogen (one proton + one electron) is neutral for the
whole plane and Q_n=-Q_nu. For fixed h=3, q=1+6n gives |Q_n/Q_e| =
3|n|/|1+3n|. For n>=1 this is at least 3/4, equality at n=1; for n<=-1
it exceeds 1. This is an exact gap for all integers, NOT a finite scan.

The measured estimate is (-0.4 ± 1.1) x 10^-21 electron charges, from cold
neutron beam deflection in a 9 m electric field region: Baumann, Gähler,
Kalus and Mampe (1988), https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.37.3107 .
We compare magnitudes and quoted uncertainty; no absolute limit, confidence
level, or Gaussian likelihood is inferred. The only fixed-h=3 lattice
member within the quoted interval is n=0. This is empirical discrimination
of a supplied model family, not a first-principles determination of charge.

If only the quotient is fixed, q=1+6n, h=3q+6 (n>=0) gives a primitive
integer character assignment with exactly the same Z6 kernel, yet signed
Q_n/|Q_e|=-1/(q+1). These are inequivalent ratios, not rescalings. Every
finite neighborhood of zero contains nonzero examples; no fitted candidate
or physical preference for very large weights is asserted.

Bressi et al.'s independent acoustic bulk-matter measurement is NOT another
direct neutron measurement. Its standard single-parameter reduction assumes
charge conservation in neutron beta decay AND antineutrino neutrality (intro
after Eq. 1, https://arxiv.org/html/1102.2766 ). The latter fails for these
nonzero examples. The raw observable can still be analyzed under a specified
composition model; their converted limit is not used here.

def near_zero(n: int) -> F:
    require(n >= 0, "nonnegative sequence parameter")
    q = 1 + 6 * n
    h = 3 * q + 6
    # gcd(q,h)=gcd(q,6)=1. A common positive rescaling cannot explain this family.
    # Also (2h)-(3q+h)=6 and both are multiples of 6: exactly six kernel elements.
    require(gcd(q, h) == 1 and 2 * h - (3 * q + h) == 6, "primitive coprime control")
    check_quotient(q, h)
    ratio = readout(q, h).neutron_in_electron_units()
    require(ratio == -F(1, q + 1), "variable-weight family")
    return ratio

Do NOT assume off-diagonal Yukawa entries, Majorana masses or a complete
mixing graph. Instead supply (1) an exactly conserved, unbroken U(1), (2)
source and detection flavor states of definite charges x_alpha and x_beta,
(3) propagation with no transfer of this charge to an unobserved environment,
and (4) the usual interpretation of the reported backgrounds, calibrated
source and charged-current tags. For a neutral-transfer channel each Kraus
operator K preserves the charge blocks: (x_beta-x_alpha) K[beta,alpha]=0.
Since P(beta|alpha) is a sum of nonnegative |K[beta,alpha]|², nonzero
support requires equal charges. This is a selection rule, not an inference
from conserved mean charge or covariance of a reduced channel alone.

Historical inputs from different collaborations, beams, detectors and
appearance channels (not two replications of the same transition):

  T2K, Phys. Rev. Lett. 112, 061802 (2014), mu -> e. 28 final candidates
  from 377 fully contained fiducial-volume events at Super-Kamiokande,
  6.57 x 10^20 protons on target. The no-appearance comparison (theta13=0)
  expects 4.92 +/- 0.55 events. Reported significance: 7.3 sigma.
  https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.112.061802
  https://arxiv.org/html/1311.4750 (event selection and background comparison)

  OPERA, Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015), mu -> tau. Five candidates
  among 5,408 analyzed interactions in the CNGS sample, including tau decay
  topology. Total background expectation 0.25 +/- 0.05; reported 5.1 sigma.
  https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.115.121802
  https://arxiv.org/html/1507.01417 (Tables 1 and 3; significance analysis)

The candidate/selection counts are not incident neutrino counts; their
ratios are not transition probabilities. Significances are the authors',
not reconstructed or combined here. Real beams are ensembles: the two
conditional positive-support inputs follow the published signal-vs-background
interpretations, not a claim that every candidate was an oscillated neutrino.

The two links connect all three active neutrinos. A common W charge and
charge-conserving calibrated vertex then transfer equality to their active
charged-lepton partners. This removes family *differences in these charges*,
not a common shift (e.g. B-L in a theory admitting it), nor does it classify
sterile fields or all gauge symmetries. Broken U(1)s, additional detection
interactions, mis-tagged or non-charge-sharp states, and charge exchange
with a reservoir are outside the implication. Exact finite controls below
exhibit a conserving exchange and inequivalent same-charge propagation with
identical flavor tables. They do not fit rates or derive neutrino dynamics.
The quantum-channel rule, sector dictionary and empirical links are supplied,
